text:
Nora (support): FYI escalated ticket from AcmeCorp — sudden 502s for their hosted inference endpoint starting ~15:12 UTC. They see a bunch of `TLS handshake timeout` and `502 Bad Gateway` in front of our API. Customer says it started right after a cert rotation window.
Jordan (netops): Can you paste the client logs? Are we seeing upstream 502s from the gateway or connection resets?
Nora (support): Pasted parts below from customer's kube sidecar logs: 
```
2026-03-15T15:12:03Z WARN api-proxy: tls handshake timeout (peer=redwood-edge-3.acme.net)
2026-03-15T15:12:04Z ERROR http: upstream returned 502 for /v1/infer
2026-03-15T15:12:06Z INFO connection: retrying with different resolver
```
They also ran `curl -v` and saw `SSL_connect:SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL in connection to api.redwood.example:443` and `no peer certificate` on some attempts.
Jordan (netops): Hmm. Similar reports from a few other customers in EU region. Any signs of A record flaps or LB target changes? Can we get `dig +short SRV _redwood._tcp.api.redwood.example` and `dig +trace` from their VPC?
Nora (support): Customer ran `dig` and sent output — SRV response seems to rotate through 3 targets (edge-1, edge-2, edge-3) with low TTL 30s. They attached a tcpdump snippet showing repeated SYN then no TLS ClientHello to one of the endpoints.
Omar (backend): Possible race during cert rotation: some edge nodes have new cert chain, others old, and if resolvers rotate mid-client backoff you can hit nodes that haven't loaded the full chain or are still reloading keystore -> handshake timeouts. Also SRV ordering + client resolver shuffling can make it appear intermittent.
Ingrid S.: We pushed cert assets in a rolling fashion earlier today. I see edge-2 completed rotation at 15:10, edge-3 at 15:14 per deploy logs. There's a small window where resolvers could be split.
deploy-bot: cert-rotation/2026-03-15 triggered by infra@redwood - rollout started at 2026-03-15T15:00Z; node edge-3 completed at 2026-03-15T15:14Z
Jordan (netops): That timing matches. Customer traffic at 15:12 could have hit edge-3 while it was still loading the new certs -> handshake timeouts. Couple action items: 1) short-term: rollback edge-3 cert or re-trigger completion so it has full chain loaded; 2) ask customers to flush DNS caches / backoff resolver; 3) consider increasing client-side TLS handshake timeout during rotation.
Omar (backend): Short-term mitigation I can do: mark edge-3 out of the SRV pool (weight=0) for 10m via netops control plane so new connections won't be routed. Can someone authorize?
Ingrid S.: Authorize. I'll also re-trigger the cert loader on edge-3 to ensure chain file present.
Jordan (netops): On the DNS side we should smooth SRV rotations — increase TTL to 120s during rollouts and add a tiny jitter on SRV ordering so not all resolvers flip at once. I'll file a followup.
Nora (support): Communicated to customer: "we're marking one edge out and reloading certs; can you retry and share a fresh `curl -v` if you still see errors". They replied: "errors reduced but intermittent 502s persist for some requests — seems correlated with specific client IP ranges."
Omar (backend): That screams resolver caching differences across ISPs. If ISP A cached SRV->edge-3 and ISP B cached edge-1, and edge-3 was flaky, you'll see IP-range correlation. We should also check our health-check spikes and any transient 5xx counts in the last 30m.
Jordan (netops): Pulled edge health metrics: edge-3 had elevated TLS handshake time p50->p95 during 15:08-15:16 and 502 spike aligns. I just set `weight=0` on edge-3 SRV and removed it from LB rotation; watch metrics.
Ingrid S.: Cert loader re-run completed, verified chain with `openssl s_client -connect edge-3:443 -showcerts` returns expected chain and no verify errors.
Nora (support): Customer confirms much better now — only a couple of residual 502s. They ran `dig +short` and saw target list now: edge-1, edge-2 (edge-3 absent).
Omar (backend): Followups: add pre-check in cert rollout that verifies chain availability on all nodes before updating DNS/SRV records; add a canary TTL strategy (longer TTL during rollout), and add a health-check gating that prevents node entering SRV pool until TLS established on 3 consecutive checks.
Jordan (netops): I'll create a postmortem/ops ticket for SRV rotation policy and rollout gating. Also recommend adding more visibility in Console: per-node cert status + TLS handshake failure rate.
Nora (support): Filing summary to customer and marking as escalated resolved pending monitoring: include repro steps we used: 
1) Simulate partial rotation by toggling cert on one edge.
2) Run `dig _redwood._tcp.api.redwood.example SRV` and note rotation.
3) From client: `curl -v --resolve api.redwood.example:443:<edge-ip> https://api.redwood.example/v1/infer` to force target & observe handshake behavior.
Example curl output we used: 
```
* About to connect() to 10.23.45.67 port 443 (#0)
*   Trying 10.23.45.67...
* Connected to 10.23.45.67 (10.23.45.67) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.3 (OUT), TLS handshake, Client hello (1):
* OpenSSL SSL_connect: SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL in connection to 10.23.45.67:443\n```
Nora (support): Customer accepted remediation and will monitor. Leaving open for 24h to ensure stability. If anyone wants to add notes to the follow-up ticket, ping me. :thumbsup:
Omar (backend): Adding doc draft for rollout checklist.
Jordan (netops): Filed NETOPS-1347 SRV-rollout-gating and added proposed TTL change.
Ingrid S.: Will run a targeted smoke test for next rotation window.
Nora (support): Thanks all. Will update ticket and close after 24h if stable. :white_check_mark:
